Troubled by lice at Hudaybiyyah, Ka'b bin Ujra was told to shave and fast three days, feed six poor people or slaughter a sheep; the verse came about him.
A man who had intercourse with his wife while fasting could not free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor, so fed his family dates given for expiation.
A man who had intercourse while fasting in Ramadan could not free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor, so dates given for expiation went to his family.
Ibn Abbas says a man who tells his wife 'You are unlawful to me' must make expiation, the Prophet being the example to follow.
Unable to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty poor after intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man was given dates as expiation and allowed to keep them.
A man who had intercourse while fasting in Ramadan could not free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, so the smiling Prophet gave him dates to keep.
Lice-troubled Ka'b could expiate by fasting, charity or sacrifice; for intercourse while fasting in Ramadan, a man unable to free a slave, fast or feed sixty fed his family.
A man who had intercourse with his wife while fasting in Ramadan, told to free a slave, fast two months or feed sixty, was given food for his family.
